newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Cook meets Japan's Ikeda in London.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Cook meets Japan's Ikeda in London.

text.p: Japan's Foreign Minister Yukihido Ikeda met Britain's new foreign minister Robin Cook for lunch on Saturday and talks on the future of Hong Kong and other issues.
A Foreign Office spokesman said the two ministers discussed a wide range of issues, including Hong Kong, NATO enlargement, the reform of the United Nations and the fight against terrorism.
However there was no discussion of the plight of British former prisoners in Japan's wartime prison camps, a subject which British officials had earlier said Cook would raise.

A group of about 12,000 British former soldiers and others imprisoned during World War Two are pressing Tokyo to pay extra compensation for what they say was the maltreatment they suffered at the hands of the Japanese.

Japan, which paid compensation to former prisoners under a 1951 treaty, refuses to consider the demands. British officials say the terms of the treaty mean there can be no formal negotiations on the subject.
The Foreign Office said the prisoners issue was raised at official level and would be discussed at subsequent meetings between the two ministers.
Ikeda was the first foreign minister from outside Europe to visit Britain since the Labour government came to power in an election on May 1.
